findings.explanation: The SPL also alerts when feed_a_ok or feed_b_ok equals 0, which is the more likely trigger. The grouped count by `entity` is not in the SPL.
findings.suggested_fix: State all three conditions: either feed down, or modelled load after losing one feed above 100%.

findings.explanation: These fields have no SNMP OID source; feed status and the modelled load come from DCIM or a stitching job, but the text lists SNMP polling as the path and never explains how the stitched power:redundancy events are created.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the stitching job (inputs, join keys, schedule) and the source of each of the four fields.

findings.explanation: This detection overlaps UC-15.1.3 (Power Redundancy Status), which also alerts on loss of an A/B feed, without saying how they differ.
References are generic Splunk pages; none covers N+1, A/B redundancy or Uptime Institute and TIA-942 redundancy levels.
findings.quote: Splunk Documentation — Getting started with alerts
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the redundancy standard the compliance claim is based on.

findings.explanation: The scenarios are template wording with no redundancy-specific cause.
findings.quote: Scheduled automation elevates `src` without crossing `load_on_loss_of_one_pct` > 100 for UC-15.1.19.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite real causes: one feed deliberately de-energised for maintenance, a stale DCIM capacity workbook after new load is added, and a PDU reboot reporting a feed as down.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: N+1 describes redundant modules or capacity components, while the fields (feed_a_ok, feed_b_ok, load after losing one feed) describe dual-feed A/B (2N) power paths. The label and the monitoringType Compliance imply more than the detection shows.

summary: The detection looks at A/B feed health and modelled load after losing one feed, but the text calls it N+1 compliance, omits the feed checks in the description, and relies on a DCIM-modelled field the SNMP path cannot supply.
